name: EUSO-SPB2
full_name: Extreme Universe Space Observatory on a Super Pressure Balloon 2
summary: A balloon-borne pathfinder tested complementary fluorescence and Cherenkov telescopes for future cosmic-ray and tau-neutrino observation from above the atmosphere.
physics_targets: Instrumentation and backgrounds for future tau-neutrino searches
detection_principle: The downward fluorescence telescope searched for cosmic-ray tracks, while the horizon-pointing Cherenkov telescope tested fast air-shower observations and backgrounds relevant to future tau-neutrino searches.

sites.name: Wanaka balloon launch
sites.location: South Pacific balloon flight from Wanaka, New Zealand

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: NASA gives the completed flight interval and explicitly states premature termination from a balloon leak.

timeline.event: Flight ended prematurely after a balloon leak.

collaboration.name: EUSO-SPB2 Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Flight
key_parameters.value: 13–15 May 2023; approximately 1.5 days before premature termination

results.summary: The mission provided instrumental and background data despite a short flight; no confirmed astrophysical tau-neutrino detection is claimed here.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
